findings.highlight: you know I enjoy cleaning up others' messes
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の仕切り癖を知ってて俺に振るお前が悪い
findings.explanation: Haruki blames Takeya for handing him the task despite knowing his compulsive habit of taking charge and organizing things. The English recasts that executive compulsion as enjoying the cleanup of other people's messes, changing both the trait and his attitude toward it.
findings.japanese: 「俺の仕切り癖を知ってて俺に振るお前が悪い！」
findings.todokanai: "It's your fault for throwing it my way when you know I enjoy cleaning up others' messes!"

findings.highlight: I simply don't want to leave any regrets on the stage…
findings.evidenceJa: ただ純粋に、ステージに穴を開けたくなくて
findings.explanation: Haruki's stated practical motive is not wanting an empty hole in the festival stage program. The English turns that staffing obligation into the sentimental abstraction of leaving regrets onstage.
findings.japanese:
「何度も言うけど、そう言うんじゃないから。
ただ純粋に、ステージに穴を開けたくなくて。
…お前の言うとおり、学園最後の思い出作りだし」
findings.todokanai: "I've told you many times already, that's not how it is. I simply don't want to leave any regrets on the stage… I want to create fond memories of the last of my school days, just like you said."

findings.highlight: there's the old saying
findings.evidenceJa: 恋する漢は百万馬力なのかもしれないけど
findings.explanation: Takeya tentatively improvises that a man in love may have extraordinary power. Todokanai TL converts the remark into an established ‘old saying,’ adding authority and quotation structure absent from the Japanese and changing the comic beat. Rendering the hyperbole as ‘the strength of a million horses’ is not itself treated as erroneous.
findings.japanese:
「いや、まぁ…
恋する漢は百万馬力なのかもしれないけど」
findings.todokanai: "Well… there's the old saying, 'A man in love has the strength of a million horses.'"

findings.highlight: I had to do so many things just to preserve my image…
findings.evidenceJa: 後はそのイメージを守るために見栄に見栄を重ねて
findings.explanation: Haruki repeats Setsuna's exact admission that she piled one act of keeping up appearances upon another, now recognizing the same trap in his own lie. The generic “did so many things” again deletes the accumulating pretense and weakens the explicit self-comparison.
findings.japanese:
『そうなると、
後はそのイメージを守るために見栄に見栄を重ねて…』
findings.todokanai: "When that happened, I had to do so many things just to preserve my image…"

findings.highlight: In order to get others interested in me, I'm leaving misunderstandings as they are, and slowly driving myself into a corner.
findings.evidenceJa: 相手に気に入られたくて、いい顔して、向こうの勘違いをそのまま放置して、どんどん追い込まれていって
findings.explanation: The pattern is wanting to be liked, putting on an agreeable face, leaving the other person's misunderstanding intact, and becoming trapped. The English turns being liked into attracting interest and omits the crucial performance of showing a pleasing face—the behavior Haruki has just recognized in both Setsuna and himself.
findings.japanese:
相手に気に入られたくて、いい顔して、
向こうの勘違いをそのまま放置して、
どんどん追い込まれていって。
findings.todokanai: In order to get others interested in me, I'm leaving misunderstandings as they are, and slowly driving myself into a corner.

findings.highlight: was in desperate need of such abilities.
findings.evidenceJa: その実力は、喉から食指のついた手が出てくるほどで
findings.explanation: Haruki deliberately crashes together 喉から手が出る, wanting something so badly a hand emerges from one's throat, and 食指が動く, one's index finger twitching with appetite. The generic “desperate need” preserves only the conclusion and deletes the grotesque mixed-idiom joke.
findings.japanese:
ギターしかいない俺たち軽音楽同好会にとって、
その実力は、喉から食指のついた手が出てくるほどで。
findings.todokanai: Our Light Music Club, which currently only has guitarists, was in desperate need of such abilities.

findings.highlight: my first impression of his crowd was right on the mark.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺のその第一印象は、まるっきり正鵠を得ていたことを痛感させられた
findings.explanation: After speaking with Matsukawa, Haruki finds his first impression of that individual—nervous-looking and difficult—exactly correct. “His crowd” invents a collective referent and misdirects the evaluation from Matsukawa to the music students generally.
findings.japanese:
…で、ちょっと話してみただけで、俺のその第一印象は、
まるっきり正鵠を得ていたことを痛感させられた。
findings.todokanai: …And after talking with him for a little bit, my first impression of his crowd was right on the mark.

findings.highlight: They'd give unpleasant looks
findings.evidenceJa: 気まずそうに目をそらしたり
findings.explanation: The music students awkwardly avert their eyes when the room is mentioned, behavior that suggests concealed knowledge. The English has them give unpleasant looks instead, reversing the direction of the gaze and changing discomfort into hostility.
findings.japanese:
なんだか、やけに触れたくない話題のようで、
気まずそうに目をそらしたり、
関わり合いになるのを恐れたり。
findings.todokanai: It seemed like they didn't want to touch the subject. They'd give unpleasant looks, and would try not to get involved.

findings.highlight: A piano that echoes… and nobody knows anything…
findings.evidenceJa: 誰も使っていないはずの音楽室。鳴り響くピアノ。そして、口を閉ざす生徒たち
findings.explanation: Haruki's school-mystery montage ends with students who close their mouths—an image of deliberate silence after their averted eyes. “Nobody knows anything” turns that suspicious refusal to speak into simple ignorance.
findings.japanese:
誰も使っていないはずの音楽室。
鳴り響くピアノ。
そして、口を閉ざす生徒たち。
findings.todokanai: No one should even be using that music room. A piano that echoes… and nobody knows anything…

findings.highlight: Listen and shudder!
findings.evidenceJa: 聞いて驚け
findings.explanation: Haruki says “Listen and be amazed,” setting up Kazusa's reply that she will not listen and therefore will not be amazed. “Shudder” supplies the wrong reaction and turns his boast into something ominous.
findings.japanese:
「聞いて驚け。
なんとあの…」
findings.todokanai: "Listen and shudder! It turns out she's…"

findings.highlight: In the end, I'd also slept through my usual practice time.
findings.evidenceJa: 結局、いつもの練習時間まで居座ってしまった
findings.explanation: It is just past five, and Haruki realizes he has ended up lingering in the classroom until his usual practice time. The English says he slept through the practice period, falsely implying that the time has already passed and that he missed it.
findings.japanese:
時計を見ると、何だかんだでもう５時を過ぎてる。
結局、いつもの練習時間まで居座ってしまった。
findings.todokanai: Looking at the time, it seems like it's just past five. In the end, I'd also slept through my usual practice time.

findings.highlight: a sound that was casual, profound, elegant, and stubborn
findings.evidenceJa: 軽快で、重厚で、流麗で、頑強な音
findings.explanation: Haruki describes the playing as brisk, weighty, fluid, and robust. “Casual” and especially “stubborn” are not musical equivalents for 軽快 and 頑強, so the English distorts the four-part description of the pianist's sound at the moment he encounters the instrument itself.
findings.japanese:
ほんのついさっきまで、いつものように、
軽快で、重厚で、流麗で、頑強な音を奏でてたのか。
findings.todokanai: Just a moment ago, as usual, he was playing with a sound that was casual, profound, elegant, and stubborn.

findings.highlight: my chance at almost catching the owner of Music Room 2
findings.evidenceJa: 『第二音楽室の主』の尻尾を掴むチャンス
findings.explanation: Haruki says he squandered a chance to catch the pianist's tail—that is, to get a lead on the person's identity. The English turns the missed chance for a clue into having almost caught the person outright.
findings.japanese:
とどめに『第二音楽室の主』の尻尾を掴むチャンスを、
自らのポカで棒に振ってしまった。
findings.todokanai: And wasting my chance at almost catching the owner of Music Room 2, through my own blunder.

findings.highlight: that fine thread
findings.evidenceJa: たった一つの蜘蛛の糸を掴み取った
findings.explanation: The source pointedly calls his last hope 蜘蛛の糸, “the spider's thread,” invoking Akutagawa's story and its single thread of salvation. “That fine thread” removes the title phrase and therefore the literary image that organizes Haruki's sudden reversal from failure to hope.
findings.japanese:
だけど、そのポカの果て。
最後の最後の最後に、
たった一つの蜘蛛の糸を掴み取った。
findings.todokanai: But, at the end of that blunder, right at the end of it all, I'd grabbed that fine thread.

findings.highlight: I'll catch you next time
findings.evidenceJa: 今度こそ、会える。会ってみせる
findings.explanation: Haruki resolves that next time he will meet the pianist—he will make the meeting happen. “Catch you” changes the desired encounter into capturing or apprehending the person, extending the previous clue metaphor into an action the Japanese does not state.
findings.japanese:
「今度こそ、会える。
会ってみせる」
findings.todokanai: "I'll catch you next time. I'll make sure of it."

findings.highlight: a complacent human being who was wary and securely locked the door during practice time. Yet he forgot to lock the door and window
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の練習中には厳重に鍵をかけるくせに、帰るときには施錠どころか窓を閉めることすら忘れる、用心深いくせに無頓着な人間
findings.explanation: Haruki constructs a paradoxical person: extremely cautious during practice, yet so careless on leaving that they forget not merely to lock up but even to close the window. “Complacent” is the wrong trait, and the English changes failure to close the window into failure to lock a window, blunting both the physical clue and the cautious/careless contrast.
findings.japanese:
自分の練習中には厳重に鍵をかけるくせに、
帰るときには施錠どころか窓を閉めることすら忘れる、
用心深いくせに無頓着な人間、だ。
findings.todokanai: He was just a complacent human being who was wary and securely locked the door during practice time. Yet he forgot to lock the door and window when heading home.

findings.highlight: people say 'fool around while you're still young,' right?
findings.evidenceJa: 『若いうちの馬鹿は買ってでもしろ』って言うだろ？
findings.explanation: Haruki has deliberately corrupted the fixed proverb 若いうちの苦労は買ってでもせよ, replacing youthful hardship with youthful stupidity, so that Takeya agrees before Haruki springs the correction. The English supplies an ordinary-sounding maxim instead of a visibly mangled proverb, leaving “No they don't” without the source joke's mechanism.
findings.japanese:
「それに…
『若いうちの馬鹿は買ってでもしろ』って言うだろ？」
findings.todokanai: "Besides, people say 'fool around while you're still young,' right?"

findings.highlight: move along the rain gutter between classrooms, and then jump to new footing at the other classroom
findings.evidenceJa: まずは教室と教室の間にある雨どいに移り、そこを新たな足場として向こうの教室の窓に飛び移る
findings.explanation: The plan is to transfer onto the rain gutter, use it as the new foothold, and then cross to the other classroom's window. The English instead has Haruki move along the gutter and treats the other classroom as the new footing, reversing the staging of the dangerous crossing.
findings.japanese:
まずは教室と教室の間にある雨どいに移り、
そこを新たな足場として向こうの教室の窓に飛び移る。
findings.todokanai: For starters, I should move along the rain gutter between classrooms, and then jump to new footing at the other classroom.

findings.highlight: my body would smash into the wall
findings.evidenceJa: もし手が離れたら全身ズルむけだな
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines the rough wall stripping the skin from his whole body if his hands slip. The English replaces that specific, tactile consequence with simply smashing into the wall, losing the payoff to his observation that the surface is rough.
findings.japanese:
いくら命綱があっても、
もし手が離れたら全身ズルむけだな…
findings.todokanai: Even if I have a lifeline, should I lose my grip, my body would smash into the wall…

findings.highlight: control my breath, and reach for the window
findings.evidenceJa: 息を整える間もなく、隣の教室の窓に手を伸ばす
findings.explanation: Haruki reaches for the next window without even pausing to steady his breathing. The English says that he controls his breath before reaching, reversing the haste that follows the gutter's alarming creak.
findings.japanese:
雨どいに全身を預けたときの嫌な軋み音を
聞かなかったことにするため、
息を整える間もなく、隣の教室の窓に手を伸ばす。
findings.todokanai: As soon as I put my entire body weight on the rain gutter, I hear a disturbing, creaking sound. I do my best to ignore it, control my breath, and reach for the window of the next classroom.

findings.highlight: Sensitive, with a small face
findings.evidenceJa: 線が細く、顔も小さく
findings.explanation: 線が細い describes the pianist's slight, slender build. “Sensitive” is not a physical description and invents a personality judgment just as Haruki is visually assembling the unknown pianist's identity.
findings.japanese:
線が細く、顔も小さく、
何より、その横顔の白さ。
findings.todokanai: Sensitive, with a small face, and most importantly, the paleness of the face from the side.

findings.highlight: wiping away all those minor details, what absolutely enthralls me is that strong melody
findings.evidenceJa: それらのか細いイメージを一掃する、俺の耳を叩く力強い旋律
findings.explanation: The powerful melody striking Haruki's ears sweeps away the preceding impression of physical slightness and fragility. The English demotes those visual impressions to “minor details” and invents enthrallment, breaking the deliberate contrast between the small figure and the force of her playing.
findings.japanese:
けれど、それらのか細いイメージを一掃する、
俺の耳を叩く力強い旋律。
findings.todokanai: However, wiping away all those minor details, what absolutely enthralls me is that strong melody ringing in my ears.

findings.highlight: may or may not be a violation of the school rules
findings.evidenceJa: いくつの校則を違反しているか定かでない行為
findings.explanation: There is no doubt that Haruki is violating school rules; the joke is that he cannot tell how many. The English changes uncertainty about the number of violations into uncertainty about whether any violation occurred at all.
findings.japanese:
俺の、いくつの校則を違反しているか定かでない行為は、
とうとう、校内で然るべき責任を持つ人たちの
知ることとなり。
findings.todokanai: My actions, which may or may not be a violation of the school rules, are found out by the school staff.

findings.highlight: is none other than my neighboring student
findings.evidenceJa: 放課後のお隣さんの、これが正体
findings.explanation: Kazusa is revealed as Haruki's “neighbor after school”—the unknown pianist in the room next door. The next line then identifies her as his neighbor during class, joining the two meanings of 隣 that the scene has kept separate. Calling her merely a neighboring student collapses the first half of that paired reveal into the classroom relation.
findings.japanese:
『第二音楽室の主』。
放課後のお隣さんの、これが正体。
findings.todokanai: The owner of Music Room 2… is none other than my neighboring student.
